title: Атопия и хронический зуд
terminology: Atopy is a clinical diagnosis after sequential exclusion of plausible pruritic disease, not a single allergy test result.
Intradermal or serum allergen-specific IgE indicates sensitization/exposure and is primarily used to select history-compatible allergens for immunotherapy after clinical diagnosis.
Breed, age, Favrot criteria and anti-inflammatory response change probability but never prove disease alone.
Canine atopic dermatitis, feline atopic skin syndrome, food-induced disease, flea/parasite/contact overlap and secondary infection remain separate evidence components.
More than one trigger may coexist only in authored compatible combinations.
No fleas seen on one exam does not exclude flea-allergy dermatitis.
Reaction patterns such as miliary dermatitis or eosinophilic lesions are not etiologic diagnoses.
Food allergy requires a strict elimination and controlled provocation pathway; serum or saliva food tests do not replace it.
Site-specific skin and ear cytology is interpreted with lesions and does not become a universal body result.
Secondary infection can amplify itch without erasing underlying allergy.
No drug, dose, taper, diet recipe, allergen mixture or immunotherapy schedule is generated.

commonHistoryQuestions.prompt: Когда начался зуд и что/где было первым?
Был ли зуд до высыпаний или инфекции?
Где лижет, чешет, трёт или выкусывает и есть ли video?
Есть ли months, environment или сезонные flare windows?
Чем, когда и у всех ли животных проводится flea control?
Есть ли dated/site-specific scraping, cytology или culture?
Что именно ел пациент, включая treats, flavored medicines и shared bowls?
Есть ли stool/vomiting/GI signs и какова частота?
Что менялось: cleaners, grass, bedding, litter, move или insects?
Какие компоненты помогали, насколько и на какой срок?
Есть ли adverse effects или подтверждённые comorbidities?
Что владелец и пациент реально могут выполнять?

variants.title: Собачий атопический дерматит: средовой паттерн
variants.diagnosticTruth: Canine atopic dermatitis is a compatible pruritic phenotype established clinically after exclusion and control of parasites, infection, food reaction and other mimics; seasonality, breed and Favrot criteria modify probability only.

presentations.complaint: Seasonal recurrent itch affects face, feet, ears and flexures, with licking and rubbing before secondary lesions.

historyAnswers.onset_first_site_date: Itch began at paws/face before lesions.

examFindings.finding: Face, paws, pinnae and flexures mapped.
Sequential workup remains mandatory.

investigations.result: Secondary infection status by sampled site.

followUp.timing: after exclusion/control checkpoints and again in the same season scale

outcomes.safe: Environmental atopy remains a clinical longitudinal conclusion with separated contributors.
outcomes.unsafe: Season, breed or one test alone unlocks the diagnosis.

ownerCommunication: Explain that the distribution guides the workup but does not replace it.

presentations.complaint: Chronic year-round pruritus has seasonal worsening and incomplete response to prior symptom control.

historyAnswers.seasonality_flare_windows: Baseline itch plus reproducible flare window.
historyAnswers.prior_components_and_response: Partial temporary relief; no proof of etiology.
historyAnswers.complete_recent_diet_exposures: Diet exposure inventory incomplete until asked.

examFindings.finding: Response is one longitudinal clue only.
Multiple authored components are assessed separately.

followUp.timing: component-by-component checkpoints across baseline and flare

outcomes.safe: Chronic and seasonal components are disentangled before long-term control is chosen.
outcomes.unsafe: Incomplete symptom response becomes diagnostic failure or automatic escalation.

ownerCommunication: Show which component is being tested at each checkpoint.

presentations.complaint: Recurrent otitis is the dominant manifestation, with subtle paw or facial itch between ear flares.

historyAnswers.onset_first_site_date: Ear episodes preceded obvious generalized lesions.
historyAnswers.prior_scraping_cytology_culture: Prior ear treatment lacked consistent site cytology.

examFindings.finding: Ear and skin components mapped separately.
Current ear sampled rather than old generic result reused.

followUp.timing: ear recheck plus later whole-patient allergy checkpoint

outcomes.safe: The ear episode is resolved and recurrence is connected to a validated whole-patient plan.
outcomes.unsafe: Every recurrent ear is labeled generic allergy without examination or cytology.

ownerCommunication: Explain why each ear flare needs current evidence and why recurrence needs a broader plan.

variants.title: Кошачий атопический кожный синдром
variants.diagnosticTruth: Feline atopic skin syndrome is diagnosed after excluding and separating flea, food, parasite, infection and other causes; alopecia, miliary dermatitis and eosinophilic patterns are reaction patterns rather than etiologies.

presentations.complaint: Cat has head-neck pruritus or apparently symmetrical alopecia caused by repeated grooming.

examFindings.finding: Broken hairs and home behavior support self-trauma.
No single visible cause is assumed.

investigations.result: Feline pruritus and reaction pattern map.

followUp.timing: after each exclusion trial using home video and same body map

outcomes.safe: Pruritus is recognized and causes are tested without turning alopecia into an etiology.
outcomes.unsafe: Alopecia is assumed behavioral or atopic without exclusion workup.

ownerCommunication: Explain that grooming can hide itch and that the pattern does not name the trigger.

presentations.complaint: Miliary papules or an eosinophilic lesion pattern accompanies pruritus, but the underlying trigger is not yet known.

historyAnswers.household_flea_control_inventory: Exposure remains possible even without seen fleas.
historyAnswers.complete_recent_diet_exposures: Food route not presumed or excluded.

examFindings.finding: Morphology is documented as a reaction pattern.
Refractory morphology does not remain generic allergy.

followUp.timing: morphology and trigger checkpoint after initial workup

outcomes.safe: Reaction pattern is separated from etiology and atypical disease is escalated.
outcomes.unsafe: Eosinophilic or miliary appearance is treated as proof of one allergy.

ownerCommunication: Name the skin pattern while being explicit that several causes can produce it.

presentations.complaint: Cat has intermittent pruritus with sparse lesions and plausible flea, food, environmental or stress modifiers, none individually proven.

examFindings.finding: Overlap is not randomly generated.
Video and repeat map retained.

outcomes.safe: Only evidence-supported overlap is retained and the plan remains measurable.
outcomes.unsafe: Random multi-allergy labeling produces untestable polytherapy.

ownerCommunication: Explain why a staged plan is more informative than changing everything at once.

variants.title: Пищеиндуцированный аллергический дерматит
variants.diagnosticTruth: A food-induced allergic skin component is evaluated with a complete exposure history, strict feasible elimination trial and controlled provocation when safe; year-round itch, gastrointestinal signs or improvement alone are not confirmatory.

presentations.complaint: Year-round pruritus raises a food component question; gastrointestinal signs may be present or absent.

historyAnswers.complete_recent_diet_exposures: Foods, treats, flavored medicines and shared bowls inventoried.
historyAnswers.gi_signs_context: GI signs recorded but not required.
historyAnswers.prior_components_and_response: Previous diet changes were not automatically valid trials.

examFindings.finding: Skin and GI evidence remain separate.
Other itch causes stay active.

followUp.timing: baseline, strict trial checkpoints and controlled challenge

outcomes.safe: Food involvement is confirmed or rejected through a measurable longitudinal route.
outcomes.unsafe: Year-round itch or GI signs alone produce a permanent food-allergy label.

ownerCommunication: Explain that food allergy cannot be confirmed by symptoms or a blood/saliva panel alone.

presentations.complaint: An apparent elimination-trial failure is complicated by hidden exposures, household logistics or an infeasible plan.

historyAnswers.complete_recent_diet_exposures: Hidden treats/flavored medicines/shared food identified or actively audited.
historyAnswers.owner_feasibility_and_handling: Budget, household and feeding separation recorded.
historyAnswers.prior_components_and_response: Trial dates and adherence gaps reconstructed.
historyAnswers.gi_signs_context: GI trend recorded on same timeline.

examFindings.finding: Exposure and duration validity are audited.
Alternative safe route offered.

investigations.result: Eligible, controlled, measurable trial or invalid status.

followUp.timing: early feasibility check then predefined trial and challenge checkpoints

outcomes.safe: Invalidity is detected and the route is redesigned or referred without blame.
outcomes.unsafe: An uncontrolled trial is called negative or the owner is blamed.

ownerCommunication: Audit the plan together and name every exposure path without moral judgment.

presentations.complaint: Pruritus improved on a valid elimination trial and reproducibly returned during a controlled, clinically safe provocation.

examFindings.finding: Baseline, improvement and relapse linked.
Residual itch is reassessed, not forced into one cause.

followUp.timing: post-provocation recovery and long-term residual-itch review

outcomes.safe: A specific food component is confirmed with a sustainable plan and residual disease review.
outcomes.unsafe: Improvement alone or an unsafe challenge becomes confirmation.

ownerCommunication: Explain what the challenge proved and what it did not prove about other triggers.

variants.title: Перекрытие с блошиным, паразитарным или контактным зудом
variants.diagnosticTruth: Flea allergy, mites, other ectoparasites, contact/insect triggers and atopy are separate components; absence of visible fleas or a negative scraping does not alone exclude them, and overlap is retained only when each component has authored evidence.

presentations.complaint: No fleas are seen today, but exposure, household control gaps and lesion distribution remain compatible with flea allergy.

historyAnswers.household_flea_control_inventory: Products, dates, all pets and environment are incomplete or reveal gaps.
historyAnswers.onset_first_site_date: Dorsolumbar/perianal or feline variable pattern recorded.
historyAnswers.prior_components_and_response: Prior inconsistent control cannot exclude disease.

examFindings.finding: Exposure and compatible distribution remain actionable.
Single-pet spot treatment is not assumed adequate.

investigations.result: Exposure, combing and controlled household response.

followUp.timing: household control checkpoint and lesion-map response

outcomes.safe: Flea component is tested through a complete household route despite a negative snapshot.
outcomes.unsafe: No flea seen closes the differential.

ownerCommunication: Explain why an allergic patient may react without fleas being found during the visit.

presentations.complaint: A mite or other ectoparasite can mimic or coexist with allergic pruritus, with variable scraping sensitivity.

historyAnswers.prior_scraping_cytology_culture: Sampling sites and prior results reviewed.

examFindings.finding: Sampling quality and compatible control trial considered.
Other affected contacts recorded.

investigations.result: Sampling plus compatible control trial where indicated.

outcomes.safe: Test limitations and household risk are integrated into a measurable route.
outcomes.unsafe: One negative scrape closes all ectoparasite differentials.

ownerCommunication: Explain the sensitivity limit and what result or response will settle the question.

presentations.complaint: Pruritus correlates with contact, insects or environment, while another allergic component remains possible but unproven.

historyAnswers.home_contact_environment_changes: Cleaner, bedding, grass, litter, insect and move timeline recorded.

examFindings.finding: Removal and re-exposure evidence needed.
No random multi-trigger label.

followUp.timing: after controlled removal and, only when safe, re-exposure observation

outcomes.safe: A contact or insect component is tested without inventing a multi-allergy diagnosis.
outcomes.unsafe: A coincidence or one improvement proves every suspected trigger.

ownerCommunication: Explain the difference between a useful exposure clue and confirmed causation.

variants.title: Вторичная инфекция или инфекционный flare
variants.diagnosticTruth: Staphylococcal pyoderma, Malassezia overgrowth and otitis can amplify allergic pruritus; current site-specific cytology guides the infection component while recurrent, deep or nonresponsive disease requires culture and underlying-cause review.

presentations.complaint: Papules, pustules, crusts or epidermal collarettes accompany a sudden increase in pruritus on a chronic allergic background.

historyAnswers.itch_before_lesions_infection: Baseline itch preceded the current infection flare.
historyAnswers.prior_components_and_response: Allergy control was partial before infection.
historyAnswers.adverse_effects_comorbidities: Comorbid risk and prior adverse effects recorded.

examFindings.finding: Representative current lesion sampled.
Allergic and other triggers remain active questions.

followUp.timing: infection response then residual itch and recurrence audit

outcomes.safe: Current infection and underlying pruritus are both tracked to resolution or referral.
outcomes.unsafe: Infection is repeatedly treated without cytology or cause review.

ownerCommunication: Explain that infection can worsen the itch but may be a consequence rather than the whole diagnosis.

presentations.complaint: Greasy, erythematous, malodorous skin or otitis accompanies increased pruritus and suspected Malassezia overgrowth.

historyAnswers.prior_scraping_cytology_culture: Prior yeast result is not reused for every site.

examFindings.finding: Site-specific cytology integrated with morphology.
Each clinically affected site sampled as needed.

outcomes.safe: Yeast significance and response are verified by site while the underlying driver remains in view.
outcomes.unsafe: A generic yeast count dictates treatment everywhere or becomes the permanent cause.

ownerCommunication: Explain why an ear result and a skin result answer different site questions.

presentations.complaint: Skin or ear infection recurs rapidly or fails an apparently appropriate reviewed plan, requiring culture, protocol audit and underlying-cause reassessment.

historyAnswers.prior_scraping_cytology_culture: Dated sites, prior organisms, susceptibility and response reconstructed.
historyAnswers.prior_components_and_response: Actual technique, completion and response audited.

examFindings.finding: Representative active site routed to culture.
Failure is not assumed to be resistance alone.

outcomes.safe: Recurrence is evidence-routed and underlying causes are corrected or referred.
outcomes.unsafe: Repeated empiric escalation continues without culture or cause audit.

ownerCommunication: Explain that recurrence can reflect biology, technique, feasibility or another disease—not personal failure.

variants.title: Продольный плохой контроль и маршрут иммунотерапии
variants.diagnosticTruth: Poor control is audited across diagnosis, current flare, parasites, food, infection, environment, technique, adherence, comorbidity and adverse effects; allergen testing is used only after clinical diagnosis to select history-compatible allergens for specialist-directed immunotherapy, whose response is delayed and longitudinal.

presentations.complaint: Previously diagnosed allergic skin disease is poorly controlled, with possible trigger exposure, technique, schedule or household-plan gaps.

historyAnswers.prior_components_and_response: Actual components, timing and response reconstructed.
historyAnswers.owner_feasibility_and_handling: Handling, budget and household burden recorded.
historyAnswers.household_flea_control_inventory: All-pet control verified rather than assumed.

examFindings.finding: Flare, infection, exposure, technique and feasibility separated.
Observed barriers lead to a feasible alternative.

followUp.timing: after one corrected barrier at a time

outcomes.safe: Correctable barriers are addressed before treatment broadening.
outcomes.unsafe: Poor control triggers blame or random escalation.

ownerCommunication: Frame the audit as redesigning the plan around real life, not testing obedience.

presentations.complaint: A previously useful control component is now limited by an adverse effect or confirmed comorbidity, while pruritus remains clinically important.

historyAnswers.adverse_effects_comorbidities: Dated effect, diagnosis and current safety state recorded.
historyAnswers.prior_components_and_response: Benefit and harm of each component separated.
historyAnswers.itch_before_lesions_infection: Current flare and infection chronology mapped.

examFindings.finding: Benefit-risk conflict is explicit.
Reviewed clinician/specialist route required.

outcomes.safe: The unsafe component is reviewed and a specialist-supported alternative preserves skin control.
outcomes.unsafe: A contraindicated component continues or the generator invents a replacement regimen.

ownerCommunication: Explain the safety boundary and why the exact alternative must be clinician-reviewed.

presentations.complaint: A clinically established, persistently burdensome atopic patient is referred for allergen testing to select history-compatible immunotherapy components.

historyAnswers.seasonality_flare_windows: Clinical exposure pattern fixed before testing.

examFindings.finding: Testing is not used as a diagnostic shortcut.
No immediate cure or generated mixture.

investigations.result: Sensitization interpreted against history for immunotherapy selection.
Delayed response on the same scale.

followUp.timing: specialist-defined delayed checkpoints with stable baseline scales

outcomes.safe: Testing is used for its proper selection role and response is judged longitudinally.
outcomes.unsafe: A positive panel diagnoses atopy or the generator composes an allergen mixture.

ownerCommunication: Explain that the test shows sensitization, not proof of disease, and that benefit is assessed over time.

familyValidationRules: Reject if breed, Favrot criteria, IgE test or treatment response alone proves atopy.
Reject if no visible flea excludes flea allergy or reaction pattern becomes etiology.
Reject if serum/saliva food test replaces elimination/provocation.
Reject if secondary infection is ignored or becomes the only diagnosis forever.
Reject if allergy testing is sold before clinical workup or immunotherapy response is instant.
Reject if code generates a drug, dose, taper, diet recipe, allergen mixture or immunotherapy schedule.
